You already know the structure. Lessons 2 and 3 showed you the exact anatomy of both file types -- a command spec and a workflow. Two files, two layers. Think about what each one contains.
Re-read Lesson 2 (Command Spec Anatomy) and Lesson 3 (Workflow Anatomy). Every structural element you need is documented there. Pay attention to the YAML frontmatter fields and the XML sections.

The two files go at specific paths in your GSD install: the command spec at ~/.claude/commands/gsd/skeptic.md and the workflow at ~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/skeptic.md. These are real files that Claude Code will find.

The command spec needs YAML frontmatter with name, description, and allowed-tools fields, plus XML sections: objective, execution_context (with an @file reference to the workflow), context, and process. The workflow needs purpose and process sections.

Create skeptic.md at ~/.claude/commands/gsd/skeptic.md. Start with YAML frontmatter: name: gsd:skeptic, a description, and allowed-tools. Then add <objective>, <execution_context> containing @~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/skeptic.md, <context>, and <process> sections. Create the workflow at ~/.claude/get-shit-done/workflows/skeptic.md with <purpose> and <process> sections. The @file reference in execution_context is the critical wiring between the two layers.
